about_p1: The Pakarina spatiotemporal platform was established in 2026 through the collaborative work of professors from the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP), the State University of Minas Gerais (UEMG), Fiocruz Minas, and the National University of San Cristóbal de Huamanga (Peru). The initiative also includes the participation of international exchange students from the Catholic University of Salta (Argentina), ISEN Yncréa Ouest (France), and Benin, a country located on the African continent.
about_p2: The platform aims to georeference arbovirus occurrences and to bring together information, tools, devices, and people that currently operate in separate environments, recognizing that the dynamics of these diseases are determined by a set of interconnected processes involving climatic, urban, environmental, and social factors.
about_p3: Climate variability influences the abundance and competence of disease vectors, while unplanned urbanization and inadequate sanitation systems increase human-vector contact. In addition, human mobility and environmental changes contribute to the spatial spread of infectious agents and to modifications in vector habitats.
about_p4: In this context, the One Health approach integrates human, animal, and environmental dimensions, highlighting that arboviruses circulate within complex and dynamic ecological networks, often involving enzootic cycles before transmission to human populations.
about_p5: Major urban arboviral diseases such as dengue, chikungunya, and Zika illustrate this complexity, as their transmission is predominantly associated with Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. From a clinical perspective, these diseases can range from mild symptoms to severe and potentially fatal outcomes.
about_p6: More recently, the Oropouche virus has attracted increasing attention due to its rapid geographic expansion across the Americas. Its transmission is mainly associated with the biting midge Culicoides paraensis, creating particularly complex epidemiological and ecological challenges for the surveillance and control of this emerging arboviral disease.
about_p7: At its core, Pakarina is developing a modern web platform capable of integrating information from sensors, monitoring devices, databases, mapping systems, external services, and educational resources, designed as a scalable and adaptable foundation.
about_p8: Our vision is to build a sustainable technological ecosystem that strengthens monitoring capabilities, improves information accessibility, and promotes collaboration between technical and non-technical stakeholders, connecting people, information, and action.
contact_intro: Pakarina is a collaborative initiative developed by the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP) in partnership with the Catholic University of Salta (UCASAL) and Yncrea. climate_temp_info: Adult mosquitoes thrive between 25°C and 35°C. Below 10°C, most adult mosquitoes cannot survive for long periods.
climate_humidity_info: Humidity above 60% promotes mosquito survival and breeding.
climate_wind_info: Wind speeds below 3 m/s allow mosquitoes to remain active and fly more easily.
climate_precipitation_info: Rainfall above 5 mm can create standing water, while rainfall above 20 mm significantly increases potential breeding sites.
climate_error: City not found. Please try again.
climate_no_data: Search a city to see the dengue risk analysis.
climate_msg_high: ⚠️ Current conditions are highly favorable for dengue mosquito proliferation. Take preventive measures.
climate_msg_medium: ⚡ Conditions partially favor mosquito activity. Stay alert and eliminate standing water.
climate_msg_low: ✅ Current conditions are not particularly favorable for dengue mosquito proliferation.
climate_temp_msg_verylow: Very low risk (< 10°C): most adult mosquitoes do not survive long under these temperatures. Be cautious if the area benefits from a warmer microclimate (heated indoor space, sheltered area).
climate_temp_msg_low: Cool temperatures (10°C < T < 20°C): mosquito activity and reproduction are slowed down, but not absent.
climate_temp_msg_medium: Moderately favorable conditions (20°C < T < 25°C): mosquito activity and reproduction gradually increase.
climate_temp_msg_high: ⚠️ 25°C < T < 35°C  => Ideal conditions for the proliferation and survival of adult mosquitoes. Stay vigilant.
climate_temp_msg_extreme: Excessive heat (> 35°C): may reduce the survival of mosquitoes and larvae. Stay vigilant nonetheless.
climate_humidity_msg_low: Dry air (0-40%): unfavorable conditions for mosquito survival, activity, and reproduction.
climate_humidity_msg_medium: Moderate humidity (40-60%): partially favorable conditions for mosquito survival, activity, and reproduction.
climate_humidity_msg_high: ⚠️ High humidity (> 60%): clearly favors mosquito survival and reproduction.
climate_wind_msg_low: Low wind (< 3m/s): mosquitoes remain active and fly easily.
climate_wind_msg_high: Sufficient wind to limit mosquito flight and activity. (> 3m/s)
climate_precip_msg_low: No significant water accumulation (0-5mm); low risk of breeding sites.
climate_precip_msg_medium: May create standing water, favoring the appearance of breeding sites. (5mm-20mm)
home_module_news: Stay informed with the latest epidemiological news on dengue, automatically collected from over 20 trusted media sources across Brazil, Argentina, Peru, France, and beyond. Filter by country, source, or date to follow what matters most.
home_module_climate: Visualize real-time weather conditions and understand how temperature, humidity, and rainfall influence dengue mosquito proliferation. Climate data is combined with environmental analysis to provide actionable risk insights.
home_module_awareness: Access educational resources, prevention guides, and awareness campaigns related to dengue. This module supports communities, schools, and institutions with clear and accessible public health information.
home_module_dashboard: Monitor the platform's key indicators through an integrated dashboard. Currently displaying live weather data for João Monlevade, the dashboard will progressively integrate sensor data, maps, and real-time alerts in future sprints.
home_hero_text: A centralized platform for dengue monitoring, data integration, and community awareness — developed at UFOP.
home_dengue_title: Dengue in Brazil — A Growing Crisis
home_dengue_text: Brazil is the country most affected by dengue in the world. In 2024, over 10 million cases were recorded — a historic record — along with nearly 6,000 deaths. The disease spreads through the Aedes aegypti mosquito and thrives in warm, humid conditions, making monitoring and prevention more critical than ever.
home_stat_source: Sources: Brazilian Ministry of Health, PAHO — 2024 data
home_summary_text: Pakarina is an interdisciplinary initiative developed at the Federal University of Ouro Preto (UFOP) in partnership with UCASAL and Yncrea. It centralizes fragmented data sources related to dengue into a single, unified web platform — improving coordination between technical teams, researchers, educators, and public health institutions.
home_mission_text: Pakarina aims to build a sustainable technological ecosystem that strengthens monitoring capabilities, improves information accessibility, and promotes collaboration between technical and non-technical participants. By combining technology, research, and community engagement, Pakarina seeks to create tools that contribute to public health, environmental awareness, and innovation-driven problem solving.

aw_intro: We carry out awareness activities in several schools with the aim of providing clear, practical, and engaging information about dengue prevention and environmental care. Through educational talks, creative activities, and interactive experiences, we encourage habits that contribute to the health and well-being of the entire community.
aw_schools_title: What Do We Do in Schools?
aw_schools_sub: Main activities of our awareness programs
aw_card1_text: Educational talks about dengue and the importance of preventing mosquito breeding sites.
aw_card2_text: How to identify and remove containers with standing water where mosquito larvae develop.
aw_card3_text: Distribution of flyers so students can share prevention practices with their families.
aw_card4_text: Interactive activities that teach students about dengue through mosquito origami.
aw_card5_text: Activities promoting environmental awareness and the importance of protecting ecosystems.
aw_card6_text: Educational activities focused on wildfire prevention and respect for local wildlife.
aw_prev_text: During the activities, students learn that the mosquito responsible for transmitting dengue can reproduce in containers with stagnant water, such as bottles, tires, flower pots, and buckets. We promote simple actions that help eliminate breeding sites and protect the community.
aw_measure3: ✅ Check tires, bottles, and flower pots
aw_measure4: ✅ Keep yards and surrounding areas clean
aw_origami_text: As part of the awareness activities, students participate in a creative mosquito origami workshop. This activity provides a visual, practical, and interactive way of learning, turning an artistic experience into an educational tool that reinforces dengue prevention messages.
aw_origami_btn: 🎥 Learn How to Make Your Own Mosquito Origami
aw_env_title: Protecting the Environment Is Also Prevention
aw_env1_text: Together with forest rangers, students learn about environmental protection and preserving local ecosystems.
aw_env2_text: Students learn how careless actions can lead to forest fires and why responsible behavior matters.
aw_env3_text: Students are introduced to regional species and encouraged to respect and protect wildlife.
aw_gallery_sub: Photos from our school awareness activities
aw_gallery_note: Photos from school visits will be added here.
aw_final_text: "Prevention starts with small actions. Learning, eliminating mosquito breeding sites, and sharing knowledge with the community are essential steps toward building healthier and safer environments for everyone."
